# A Brief History of the Marshall Scholarship

![Image 2](https://marshall-wpta.azurewebsites.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/diplomasanddiplomacythehistoryofthemarshallscholarship-170723030415-thumbnail-4-1.jpg)

In the early 1950s, as countries were navigating the political dynamics of the postwar world, the United Kingdom was eager to retain and strengthen its close association with its wartime ally, the United States. The United States had recently gifted Europe a massive amount of foreign aid through the Economic Recovery Program (ERP), better known as the Marshall Plan. The UK Foreign Office wanted to send a thank you.

Eventually, after considering competing proposals (such as gifting an original copy of the Magna Carta and sending chandeliers for the newly refurbished White House), the Foreign Office settled on an idea to start a UK scholarship program for American students. The man who proposed the idea, Sir Roger Mellor Makins, then Deputy Undersecretary of State, suggested the scholarship be named after the aid program’s namesake, General George C. Marshall.

Makins was himself personally connected to the United States through his American wife, Alice Brooks Davis (daughter of former U.S. Secretary of War, Dwight F. Davis). He believed in the long-term value of Anglo-American accord, and while the primary impetus behind the Marshall Scholarship was gratitude for Marshall Aid, Makins (and others) also hoped it would produce a positive effect on Anglo-American relations in perpetuity. It is for this reason that the Marshall Scholarship, unique among its peer scholarships at the time, was enshrined in an Act of Parliament – something the founders knew would be tremendously difficult to undo.

Makins’ very first pitch was a modest six two-year scholarships, open to men and women, to the University of Cambridge. Very soon, Cambridge was replaced by a free choice of university within the UK, and six scholarships became twelve. This formed the basic blueprint of the program.

After three debates within Winston Churchill’s cabinet, Secretary of State Anthony Eden presented a White Paper for the Scholarship to Parliament in May 1953. Soon after, on 31 July 1953, the Marshall Aid Commemoration Act became British law. It established the Marshall Aid Commemoration Commission (MACC) to manage the Scholarships under the chairmanship of Sir Oliver Franks, who had been British Ambassador in Washington while the Marshall Plan was in operation. By agreement, the Association of Universities of the British Commonwealth (now the Association of Commonwealth Universities) provided the secretariat for the new MACC and John Foster, the Association’s Secretary General, became the MACC’s first Executive Secretary. Makins, meanwhile, managed the process in the United States, where he had just been named Ambassador. Together, Franks, Foster, and Makins oversaw the Scholarship during its first few critical years. They filled the ranks of selection committees and the Advisory Council in Washington with high-profile and prominent Americans, who reviewed and interviewed the applications for the first Marshall Scholarships.

In the first year, seven hundred students applied for the new awards, seventy-four were interviewed, and twelve were ultimately offered Scholarships (eight men and four women). Two were Stanford graduates, with Bowdoin, Bryn Mawr, Dartmouth, Harvard, Kentucky, Oberlin, Princeton, Utah, Virginia and Wisconsin providing the remainder. Upon their arrival to the UK’s shores on the _Queen Elizabeth_ on 4 October 1954, the group was welcomed by a throng of BBC journalists looking to interview the newly-minted Scholars. Four Scholars elected to go to London (all to the London School of Economics), four to Oxford, and one each to Bristol, Cambridge, Glasgow and Manchester. Seven used their Scholarship to study for a graduate degree, the remainder a second BA.

The 1953 Act set up four regional selection committees based in New York, New Orleans, Chicago and San Francisco to interview candidates and make recommendations to a national Advisory Council chaired by the British Ambassador. The Advisory Council was to review the regional recommendations and prepare a national list of recommended candidates that it would refer to the MACC for final approval. The basic structure of the program remains the same, though some elements of the process have changed significantly. Regional selection committees still review and interview candidates, though there are now eight regional centres (instead of four) based on the Consulates General in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, New York and San Francisco and the British Embassy in Washington DC. Further, while the MACC and Advisory Council still review and approve regional committees’ recommendations, tentative offers are delivered to candidates soon after interviewing in the Fall (previously, it took until the Spring!).

In the first year, seven hundred students applied for the new awards, seventy-four were interviewed, and twelve were ultimately offered Scholarships (eight men and four women). Two were Stanford graduates, with Bowdoin, Bryn Mawr, Dartmouth, Harvard, Kentucky, Oberlin, Princeton, Utah, Virginia and Wisconsin providing the remainder. Upon their arrival to the UK’s shores on the Queen Elizabeth on 4 October 1954, the group was welcomed by a throng of BBC journalists looking to interview the newly-minted Scholars. Four Scholars elected to go to London (all to the London School of Economics), four to Oxford, and one each to Bristol, Cambridge, Glasgow and Manchester. Seven used their Scholarship to study for a graduate degree, the remainder a second BA.

Three other major changes since the inception of the Marshall program include the dramatic increase in the number of Marshall Scholarships, additional selection criteria, and (relatedly) a more diverse set of career paths of Scholarship recipients.

The number of new awards increased from twelve to twenty-four in 1960, to thirty in 1973, up to forty Scholarships in 1991, and up to forty-four between 2004 and 2007. In 2019, forty-eight Scholarships were offered.

Early selection criteria and standards favored a deeply traditional formulation of the scholar-ambassador and scholar-leader. The Scholarship – unforeseen by the founders – began producing a disproportionately large number of individuals in academia. Over 60% of Scholars from the first decade of the Scholarship spent the majority of their professional lives in higher education and research (this number jumps to 70% when part-career academics are factored in). Partly as a response, the Scholarship program, upon recognizing this trend in the 1970s, added selection criteria like “impact” and “the capacity to play an active part in [university] life” (despite the facts that academics had certainly produced impact and had participated in university life!). Over time, these two additional criteria have since morphed into “leadership potential” and “ambassadorial potential,” which are featured on the current application. Academic achievement remains an important criterion, but it is now one of three.

As a consequence of these changes in criteria and (perhaps more) as a reflection of American society itself, Marshall Scholars and their career paths have diversified immensely over the last several decades. Today the Scholarship selects candidates from a wide range of disciplines, who in turn pursue an even wider set of careers following their Scholarships. Academics are now joined by visual and performance artists, businesspeople, financiers, government servants, politicians, entrepreneurs, educators, scientists, physicians, and lawyers, among many others.

# A Brief History of the Marshall Scholarship

![Image 2](https://marshall-wpta.azurewebsites.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/diplomasanddiplomacythehistoryofthemarshallscholarship-170723030415-thumbnail-4-1.jpg)

In the early 1950s, as countries were navigating the political dynamics of the postwar world, the United Kingdom was eager to retain and strengthen its close association with its wartime ally, the United States. The United States had recently gifted Europe a massive amount of foreign aid through the Economic Recovery Program (ERP), better known as the Marshall Plan. The UK Foreign Office wanted to send a thank you.

Eventually, after considering competing proposals (such as gifting an original copy of the Magna Carta and sending chandeliers for the newly refurbished White House), the Foreign Office settled on an idea to start a UK scholarship program for American students. The man who proposed the idea, Sir Roger Mellor Makins, then Deputy Undersecretary of State, suggested the scholarship be named after the aid program’s namesake, General George C. Marshall.

Makins was himself personally connected to the United States through his American wife, Alice Brooks Davis (daughter of former U.S. Secretary of War, Dwight F. Davis). He believed in the long-term value of Anglo-American accord, and while the primary impetus behind the Marshall Scholarship was gratitude for Marshall Aid, Makins (and others) also hoped it would produce a positive effect on Anglo-American relations in perpetuity. It is for this reason that the Marshall Scholarship, unique among its peer scholarships at the time, was enshrined in an Act of Parliament – something the founders knew would be tremendously difficult to undo.

Makins’ very first pitch was a modest six two-year scholarships, open to men and women, to the University of Cambridge. Very soon, Cambridge was replaced by a free choice of university within the UK, and six scholarships became twelve. This formed the basic blueprint of the program.

After three debates within Winston Churchill’s cabinet, Secretary of State Anthony Eden presented a White Paper for the Scholarship to Parliament in May 1953. Soon after, on 31 July 1953, the Marshall Aid Commemoration Act became British law. It established the Marshall Aid Commemoration Commission (MACC) to manage the Scholarships under the chairmanship of Sir Oliver Franks, who had been British Ambassador in Washington while the Marshall Plan was in operation. By agreement, the Association of Universities of the British Commonwealth (now the Association of Commonwealth Universities) provided the secretariat for the new MACC and John Foster, the Association’s Secretary General, became the MACC’s first Executive Secretary. Makins, meanwhile, managed the process in the United States, where he had just been named Ambassador. Together, Franks, Foster, and Makins oversaw the Scholarship during its first few critical years. They filled the ranks of selection committees and the Advisory Council in Washington with high-profile and prominent Americans, who reviewed and interviewed the applications for the first Marshall Scholarships.

In the first year, seven hundred students applied for the new awards, seventy-four were interviewed, and twelve were ultimately offered Scholarships (eight men and four women). Two were Stanford graduates, with Bowdoin, Bryn Mawr, Dartmouth, Harvard, Kentucky, Oberlin, Princeton, Utah, Virginia and Wisconsin providing the remainder. Upon their arrival to the UK’s shores on the _Queen Elizabeth_ on 4 October 1954, the group was welcomed by a throng of BBC journalists looking to interview the newly-minted Scholars. Four Scholars elected to go to London (all to the London School of Economics), four to Oxford, and one each to Bristol, Cambridge, Glasgow and Manchester. Seven used their Scholarship to study for a graduate degree, the remainder a second BA.

The 1953 Act set up four regional selection committees based in New York, New Orleans, Chicago and San Francisco to interview candidates and make recommendations to a national Advisory Council chaired by the British Ambassador. The Advisory Council was to review the regional recommendations and prepare a national list of recommended candidates that it would refer to the MACC for final approval. The basic structure of the program remains the same, though some elements of the process have changed significantly. Regional selection committees still review and interview candidates, though there are now eight regional centres (instead of four) based on the Consulates General in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, New York and San Francisco and the British Embassy in Washington DC. Further, while the MACC and Advisory Council still review and approve regional committees’ recommendations, tentative offers are delivered to candidates soon after interviewing in the Fall (previously, it took until the Spring!).

In the first year, seven hundred students applied for the new awards, seventy-four were interviewed, and twelve were ultimately offered Scholarships (eight men and four women). Two were Stanford graduates, with Bowdoin, Bryn Mawr, Dartmouth, Harvard, Kentucky, Oberlin, Princeton, Utah, Virginia and Wisconsin providing the remainder. Upon their arrival to the UK’s shores on the Queen Elizabeth on 4 October 1954, the group was welcomed by a throng of BBC journalists looking to interview the newly-minted Scholars. Four Scholars elected to go to London (all to the London School of Economics), four to Oxford, and one each to Bristol, Cambridge, Glasgow and Manchester. Seven used their Scholarship to study for a graduate degree, the remainder a second BA.

Three other major changes since the inception of the Marshall program include the dramatic increase in the number of Marshall Scholarships, additional selection criteria, and (relatedly) a more diverse set of career paths of Scholarship recipients.

The number of new awards increased from twelve to twenty-four in 1960, to thirty in 1973, up to forty Scholarships in 1991, and up to forty-four between 2004 and 2007. In 2019, forty-eight Scholarships were offered.

Early selection criteria and standards favored a deeply traditional formulation of the scholar-ambassador and scholar-leader. The Scholarship – unforeseen by the founders – began producing a disproportionately large number of individuals in academia. Over 60% of Scholars from the first decade of the Scholarship spent the majority of their professional lives in higher education and research (this number jumps to 70% when part-career academics are factored in). Partly as a response, the Scholarship program, upon recognizing this trend in the 1970s, added selection criteria like “impact” and “the capacity to play an active part in [university] life” (despite the facts that academics had certainly produced impact and had participated in university life!). Over time, these two additional criteria have since morphed into “leadership potential” and “ambassadorial potential,” which are featured on the current application. Academic achievement remains an important criterion, but it is now one of three.

As a consequence of these changes in criteria and (perhaps more) as a reflection of American society itself, Marshall Scholars and their career paths have diversified immensely over the last several decades. Today the Scholarship selects candidates from a wide range of disciplines, who in turn pursue an even wider set of careers following their Scholarships. Academics are now joined by visual and performance artists, businesspeople, financiers, government servants, politicians, entrepreneurs, educators, scientists, physicians, and lawyers, among many others.

# From Ideas to Impact

Marshall Scholarships September 9, 2026

#### **Where creativity and technology call home**

![Image 2](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-2.jpeg)
On a weekday morning on Bristol's harbourside you can pass a film production office, a bar built into an old boat, murals that were not there last summer, and a building full of people working on quantum computers.

That compression is the point. Bristol is mid-size - crossable by bike in half an hour - but an unusual number of things happen inside it at once, close enough together that a postgraduate student can be in the middle of them within a fortnight of arriving.

#### **The room on the harbourside**

Halfway along that walk is [Watershed](https://www.watershed.co.uk/), a cinema and arts centre with an open-plan studio upstairs called the [Pervasive Media Studio](https://www.watershed.co.uk/studio/). It has run as a partnership between Watershed, the [University of Bristol](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/) and UWE Bristol since 2011.

On any given day it holds well over a hundred artists, technologists, small creative companies and researchers, with free lunchtime talks anyone can walk into. The work ranges from immersive performance to accessibility design to projects on climate and cities.

In most places, the creative industry and the university are separate worlds. Here they share a room, and you are invited.

#### **Why so much of this ended up here**

If you grew up watching nature documentaries, you grew up watching Bristol. _Planet Earth, Blue Planet, Frozen Planet_— all made here. The BBC Natural History Unit has been based here since 1957, and wildlife film-makers have long come through both the Unit and the University’s biological sciences. Around a third of the world’s natural history television still comes out of this region. Aardman Animations has been here since 1976, and made Wallace and Gromit down the road. Decades of that work left thousands of small operations underneath the famous names - freelancers, two-person studios, sound designers, roughly 6,000 creative businesses across the region. The distance between having an idea and finding someone to help you build it is unusually short.

#### **The engineering underneath**

Filming something nobody has filmed before is not only a creative problem. It is one of optics, low-light sensing and moving enormous quantities of data — engineering questions the University has spent decades on.

The University leads [MyWorld](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/vision-institute/myworld/), a £30 million UKRI-funded programme pairing academics with the BBC, Aardman, Bristol Old Vic and Watershed.

For students, the route in is the [Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/innovation/): eight master’s programmes across innovation, entrepreneurship, digital media and user experience design. Many are coursework-only, with no exams: live challenges set by industry partners, and a final project in which you build a venture rather than write about one. Teaching happens in studios, not lecture theatres.

#### **Twenty minutes in the other direction**

Walk the other way and the work looks completely different.

Integrated quantum photonics - the technology underneath much of modern quantum computing hardware - was invented at Bristol, and the [Quantum Engineering Technology Labs](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/qet-labs/) have since seeded roughly a third of the UK’s quantum start-ups.

On campus sits [Isambard-AI](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/research/centres/bristol-supercomputing/), the UK's most powerful supercomputer and eleventh in the world when ranked in late 2025. In its first year it carried about a thousand research projects. Access is limited, but the culture around it — technology pointed at real problems - runs through the city.

![Image 3](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-1.jpeg)
Research here also becomes companies - 46 of them venture-backed. PsiQuantum, founded by physicists from the University’s Centre for Quantum Photonics, was valued at $7 billion in 2025. Graphcore designs machine-learning processors. Ziylo, out of the chemistry department, was bought by Novo Nordisk for work on a better insulin. Altogether, companies founded on Bristol research have created around £8.5 billion in value since 2010 - fourth in the UK and highest outside Oxford, Cambridge and London.

#### **A building where the two halves meet**

This September, the University opens a new campus beside Bristol Temple Meads station: the [Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/temple-quarter-enterprise-campus/), 38,000 square metres, to host 4,600 students.

It is more than classroom space: open-access labs for quantum and deep tech companies, a start-up incubator, and industry partners sharing corridors with teaching space.

![Image 4](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image.png)
#### **The year around the work**

None of this matters if you would not enjoy living there.

Time Out named Stokes Croft and St Paul’s the world's sixth-coolest neighbourhood in 2024, the highest-ranked in the UK. This is Banksy’s city, and every summer Upfest repaints stretches of it. It gave the world Massive Attack, Portishead and Tricky. On an August morning, hundreds of hot air balloons come up off Ashton Court at dawn, and the whole city stops to look.

Ninety minutes from London by train; an hour from the Welsh coast and the Cotswolds.

For Marshall Scholars, Bristol is a [partner university](https://marshallscholarship.org/partners/partner-universities/bristol-marshall-scholarships/) with its own dedicated award, covering graduate study in any subject at master’s or doctoral level for up to two years with a possible third for doctoral work.

# From Ideas to Impact

Marshall Scholarships September 9, 2026

#### **Where creativity and technology call home**

![Image 2](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-2.jpeg)
On a weekday morning on Bristol's harbourside you can pass a film production office, a bar built into an old boat, murals that were not there last summer, and a building full of people working on quantum computers.

That compression is the point. Bristol is mid-size - crossable by bike in half an hour - but an unusual number of things happen inside it at once, close enough together that a postgraduate student can be in the middle of them within a fortnight of arriving.

#### **The room on the harbourside**

Halfway along that walk is [Watershed](https://www.watershed.co.uk/), a cinema and arts centre with an open-plan studio upstairs called the [Pervasive Media Studio](https://www.watershed.co.uk/studio/). It has run as a partnership between Watershed, the [University of Bristol](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/) and UWE Bristol since 2011.

On any given day it holds well over a hundred artists, technologists, small creative companies and researchers, with free lunchtime talks anyone can walk into. The work ranges from immersive performance to accessibility design to projects on climate and cities.

In most places, the creative industry and the university are separate worlds. Here they share a room, and you are invited.

#### **Why so much of this ended up here**

If you grew up watching nature documentaries, you grew up watching Bristol. _Planet Earth, Blue Planet, Frozen Planet_— all made here. The BBC Natural History Unit has been based here since 1957, and wildlife film-makers have long come through both the Unit and the University’s biological sciences. Around a third of the world’s natural history television still comes out of this region. Aardman Animations has been here since 1976, and made Wallace and Gromit down the road. Decades of that work left thousands of small operations underneath the famous names - freelancers, two-person studios, sound designers, roughly 6,000 creative businesses across the region. The distance between having an idea and finding someone to help you build it is unusually short.

#### **The engineering underneath**

Filming something nobody has filmed before is not only a creative problem. It is one of optics, low-light sensing and moving enormous quantities of data — engineering questions the University has spent decades on.

The University leads [MyWorld](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/vision-institute/myworld/), a £30 million UKRI-funded programme pairing academics with the BBC, Aardman, Bristol Old Vic and Watershed.

For students, the route in is the [Centre for Innovation and Entrepreneurship](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/innovation/): eight master’s programmes across innovation, entrepreneurship, digital media and user experience design. Many are coursework-only, with no exams: live challenges set by industry partners, and a final project in which you build a venture rather than write about one. Teaching happens in studios, not lecture theatres.

#### **Twenty minutes in the other direction**

Walk the other way and the work looks completely different.

Integrated quantum photonics - the technology underneath much of modern quantum computing hardware - was invented at Bristol, and the [Quantum Engineering Technology Labs](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/qet-labs/) have since seeded roughly a third of the UK’s quantum start-ups.

On campus sits [Isambard-AI](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/research/centres/bristol-supercomputing/), the UK's most powerful supercomputer and eleventh in the world when ranked in late 2025. In its first year it carried about a thousand research projects. Access is limited, but the culture around it — technology pointed at real problems - runs through the city.

![Image 3](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-1.jpeg)
Research here also becomes companies - 46 of them venture-backed. PsiQuantum, founded by physicists from the University’s Centre for Quantum Photonics, was valued at $7 billion in 2025. Graphcore designs machine-learning processors. Ziylo, out of the chemistry department, was bought by Novo Nordisk for work on a better insulin. Altogether, companies founded on Bristol research have created around £8.5 billion in value since 2010 - fourth in the UK and highest outside Oxford, Cambridge and London.

#### **A building where the two halves meet**

This September, the University opens a new campus beside Bristol Temple Meads station: the [Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/temple-quarter-enterprise-campus/), 38,000 square metres, to host 4,600 students.

It is more than classroom space: open-access labs for quantum and deep tech companies, a start-up incubator, and industry partners sharing corridors with teaching space.

![Image 4](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image.png)
#### **The year around the work**

None of this matters if you would not enjoy living there.

Time Out named Stokes Croft and St Paul’s the world's sixth-coolest neighbourhood in 2024, the highest-ranked in the UK. This is Banksy’s city, and every summer Upfest repaints stretches of it. It gave the world Massive Attack, Portishead and Tricky. On an August morning, hundreds of hot air balloons come up off Ashton Court at dawn, and the whole city stops to look.

Ninety minutes from London by train; an hour from the Welsh coast and the Cotswolds.

For Marshall Scholars, Bristol is a [partner university](https://marshallscholarship.org/partners/partner-universities/bristol-marshall-scholarships/) with its own dedicated award, covering graduate study in any subject at master’s or doctoral level for up to two years with a possible third for doctoral work.

# How to Win the Marshall Scholarship

![Image 3](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b60aba4715015833a3922de1224201f1e68f35b6dbedd0bc7eb1ecc336516bf2?s=42&d=mm&r=g)

## What is the Marshall Scholarship?

The Marshall Scholarship is one of the most prestigious graduate scholarships for international students, offering talented young Americans the chance to study at any university in the United Kingdom. The Marshall Scholarship was established in [1953](https://ur.umbc.edu/prestigious-scholarships/marshall-scholars/marshall-scholarship-guide/) as a gesture of gratitude for the Marshall Plan, which helped rebuild Europe after World War II. Merit-based scholarships such as this one foster strong ties between the US and the UK by supporting future leaders and scholars.

What is a merit-based scholarship? Merit-based scholarships are awarded for academic excellence, and they recognize outstanding achievements and potential.

In this article, we will explore everything you need to know about the Marshall Scholarship, from its significance to the application process.

### Here is an overview of what we will cover:

*   What graduate scholarships are and how they differ from undergraduate funding
*   [Eligibility](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/apply/eligibility) criteria for the Marshall Scholarship
*   Step-by-step Marshall Scholarship application process, including requirements, supporting documents, interview preparation, and key dates and deadlines
*   Compelling reasons to pursue [higher education in the UK](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/resources/higher-education-in-uk/)
*   Other postgraduate scholarships UK and global
*   How to make your Marshall Scholarship application stand out

By the end of this guide, you’ll have a better understanding of what it takes to apply for the Marshall Scholarship and how to strengthen your applications for international scholarships.

But first, let’s start by understanding what exactly a postgraduate scholarship is.

## What is a postgraduate scholarship?

Graduate scholarships are forms of financial support awarded to students pursuing advanced degrees, such as a Master’s or Doctorate degree. Undergraduate scholarships typically focus on supporting students in their initial higher education journey. Alternatively, postgraduate scholarships help recipients specialize in their chosen fields through research and advanced study. Graduate scholarships can cover a variety of costs, including tuition fees, living expenses, research costs, and other additional allowances for things like books, equipment, and travel.

If you wish to study abroad, you should do your research on graduate scholarships for international students. Resources like [Scholarship America](https://scholarshipamerica.org/) can help connect you with the right funding opportunities.

Postgraduate scholarships play a crucial role in allowing students to further their education by decreasing the financial burden that comes with it. Graduate scholarships can open doors to different opportunities for research, collaboration, and professional development, empowering students to make meaningful contributions to their fields of study and community at large.

## Marshall Scholarship Eligibility

To be eligible for the Marshall Scholarship, applicants must meet the following [requirements](https://www.nyu.edu/academics/awards-and-highlights/global-awards/scholarships/marshall-scholarship.html):

### Minimum Scholarship Requirements

*   Be a citizen of the United States at the time of application
*   Hold an undergraduate degree from an accredited college or university in the US
*   Have a minimum GPA of 3.7 (or equivalent) at the time of graduation
*   Have graduated from their undergraduate program within the past three years

Candidates for the Marshall Scholarship are evaluated based on three key criteria. The first is academic merit, which reflects demonstrated academic excellence and intellectual curiosity. The next criterion is leadership potential, shown through proven leadership skills and the capacity to influence and inspire others. Finally, applicants are evaluated by their ambassadorial potential, highlighting the ability to serve as a bridge between the US and the UK, fostering mutual understanding and cooperation.

Additionally, Marshall Scholarship applicants must secure an official endorsement from their undergraduate institution, typically from the university’s President, Provost, or Academic Dean. This endorsement is a crucial part of the application for international scholarships, as it reflects the institution’s confidence in the candidate’s abilities and potential to succeed.

Lastly, applicants for postgraduate scholarships UK must apply to a UK institution for their graduate studies. They need to list their first-choice university and intended courses on their Marshall Scholarship application and, if selected, must enroll in the programs they specified.

Before you begin applying for international scholarships, be sure to familiarize yourself with the eligibility criteria, requirements, and deadline for the best chances at securing funding.

## How to Apply to the Marshall Scholarship

Applying for the Marshall Scholarship is a multi-step process that requires careful planning and attention to detail. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you navigate the postgraduate scholarships UK application process:

### 4 Steps to Apply to the Marshall Scholarship

![Image 6: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/pexels-ketut-subiyanto-4560175-1024x683.jpg)
### **Step 1**

The first step is research and preparation. This includes exploring UK universities and programs to find those that align with your academic and career goals. During this time, you should familiarize yourself with the scholarship’s selection criteria including academic merit, leadership potential, and ambassadorial potential.

### **Step 2**

Next, it’s important to contact your undergraduate institution. Reach out to your university’s fellowship or scholarship office to express your interest in applying. They will guide you through the internal endorsement process, so be sure to adhere to any internal deadlines, which often precede the official Marshall Scholarship deadline. For example, the University of North Carolina ([UNC](https://honorscarolina.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Marshall-Scholarship-Timeline-1-1.pdf)) typically sets its campus endorsement application deadline in early August, while [Wellesley](https://www1.wellesley.edu/careereducation/resources/marshall-scholarship-rising-seniors-graduates) College’s deadline usually falls in mid-August.

### **Step 3**

Once you have secured institutional support from your undergraduate university, you can begin the online application through the official Marshall Scholarship portal. The application requires several key materials.

![Image 7: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/pexels-pixabay-159510-1024x575.jpg)
### **Personal Statement (750 words)**

The personal statement is your opportunity to share your story. This essay should detail your background, interests, and motivations. Admissions committees are looking for authenticity and depth, so reflect on formative experiences, challenges you have overcome, and how they have shaped your academic and personal journey. Consider what drives your intellectual curiosity and how your passions align with your future goals.

### **Proposed Academic Program Essay (500 words)**

In this essay, clearly articulate your chosen course of study in the UK and explain its relevance to your future goals. The committee wants to see that you have thoroughly researched your program and understand how it fits into your broader academic and professional trajectory.

### **Post-Scholarship Plan Essay (150 words)**

This brief essay should outline your plans after completing the scholarship. Be concise but also clear about how you intend to apply what you learned in the UK once you return home or pursue your next steps.

### **Leadership Essay (500 words)**

The Marshall Scholarship values strong leadership potential. Use this essay to highlight moments where you have taken initiative, inspired others, or created meaningful change. Consider both formal roles, like student government or organization leadership, and informal leadership like mentoring, advocacy, or leading projects.

### **Ambassadorial Potential Essay (500 words)**

As a Marshall Scholar, you’re expected to act as a bridge between the UK and the US. This essay should discuss how you plan to foster transatlantic relations, both during and after your time in the UK.

### **Three Letters of Recommendation**

You will need three recommendation letters, with at least two coming from academic references. These letters should speak to your intellectual ability, leadership qualities, and character.

### **Official Transcripts**

Submit certified copies of your academic records. Securing institutional endorsement is a crucial step. You must submit your completed application to your university’s endorsement committee by their specified deadline. The institution will then review your materials and decide whether to endorse your candidacy.

If you receive an endorsement, your university will submit your application to the Marshall Commission on your behalf. It’s essential to meet all deadlines, including the official submission date, which typically falls in late September.

### **Step 4**

The final stage is the interview process. Shortlisted candidates are usually invited for interviews in November. To prepare, review your application thoroughly and be ready to discuss your academic interests, leadership experiences, and ambassadorial potential.

Throughout the application process, it’s important to stay organized–keep all your materials in order and ensure they meet the specified requirements. Make sure to carefully follow all guidelines, as failure to do so may result in disqualification. Finally, maintain clear and timely communication with your referees and university officials to ensure every component of your application is completed on time.

By carefully following these steps and paying close attention to detail, you can strengthen your Marshall Scholarship application and stand out among other applicants for postgraduate scholarships UK.

![Image 3](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/b60aba4715015833a3922de1224201f1e68f35b6dbedd0bc7eb1ecc336516bf2?s=42&d=mm&r=g)

## What is the Marshall Scholarship?

The Marshall Scholarship is one of the most prestigious graduate scholarships for international students, offering talented young Americans the chance to study at any university in the United Kingdom. The Marshall Scholarship was established in [1953](https://ur.umbc.edu/prestigious-scholarships/marshall-scholars/marshall-scholarship-guide/) as a gesture of gratitude for the Marshall Plan, which helped rebuild Europe after World War II. Merit-based scholarships such as this one foster strong ties between the US and the UK by supporting future leaders and scholars.

What is a merit-based scholarship? Merit-based scholarships are awarded for academic excellence, and they recognize outstanding achievements and potential.

In this article, we will explore everything you need to know about the Marshall Scholarship, from its significance to the application process.

### Here is an overview of what we will cover:

*   What graduate scholarships are and how they differ from undergraduate funding
*   [Eligibility](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/apply/eligibility) criteria for the Marshall Scholarship
*   Step-by-step Marshall Scholarship application process, including requirements, supporting documents, interview preparation, and key dates and deadlines
*   Compelling reasons to pursue [higher education in the UK](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/resources/higher-education-in-uk/)
*   Other postgraduate scholarships UK and global
*   How to make your Marshall Scholarship application stand out

By the end of this guide, you’ll have a better understanding of what it takes to apply for the Marshall Scholarship and how to strengthen your applications for international scholarships.

But first, let’s start by understanding what exactly a postgraduate scholarship is.

## What is a postgraduate scholarship?

Graduate scholarships are forms of financial support awarded to students pursuing advanced degrees, such as a Master’s or Doctorate degree. Undergraduate scholarships typically focus on supporting students in their initial higher education journey. Alternatively, postgraduate scholarships help recipients specialize in their chosen fields through research and advanced study. Graduate scholarships can cover a variety of costs, including tuition fees, living expenses, research costs, and other additional allowances for things like books, equipment, and travel.

If you wish to study abroad, you should do your research on graduate scholarships for international students. Resources like [Scholarship America](https://scholarshipamerica.org/) can help connect you with the right funding opportunities.

Postgraduate scholarships play a crucial role in allowing students to further their education by decreasing the financial burden that comes with it. Graduate scholarships can open doors to different opportunities for research, collaboration, and professional development, empowering students to make meaningful contributions to their fields of study and community at large.

## How many students get the Marshall Scholarship?

![Image 5: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/pexels-olly-3769706-1024x683.jpg)
Each year, up to [50](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/about#:~:text=Number%20of%20Awards%3A%20Up%20to,of%20a%20third%20academic%20year.) Marshall Scholarships are awarded to outstanding students from the US. It’s important to keep in mind, however, that merit-based scholarships such as this one foster a highly competitive selection process. For example, in 2025, only [36 scholars](https://www.forbes.com/sites/michaeltnietzel/2024/12/16/thirty-six-american-students-named-marshall-scholars-for-2025/) were chosen from a pool of [983 applicants,](https://marshallscholars.org/news-and-updates/2025-marshall-scholars#:~:text=We%20look%20forward%20to%20welcoming,institutions%20across%20the%20United%20States.) highlighting the rigorous nature of the application process for these postgraduate scholarships UK and the exceptional caliber of those chosen for international scholarships.

## Marshall Scholarship Eligibility

To be eligible for the Marshall Scholarship, applicants must meet the following [requirements](https://www.nyu.edu/academics/awards-and-highlights/global-awards/scholarships/marshall-scholarship.html):

### Minimum Scholarship Requirements

*   Be a citizen of the United States at the time of application
*   Hold an undergraduate degree from an accredited college or university in the US
*   Have a minimum GPA of 3.7 (or equivalent) at the time of graduation
*   Have graduated from their undergraduate program within the past three years

Candidates for the Marshall Scholarship are evaluated based on three key criteria. The first is academic merit, which reflects demonstrated academic excellence and intellectual curiosity. The next criterion is leadership potential, shown through proven leadership skills and the capacity to influence and inspire others. Finally, applicants are evaluated by their ambassadorial potential, highlighting the ability to serve as a bridge between the US and the UK, fostering mutual understanding and cooperation.

Additionally, Marshall Scholarship applicants must secure an official endorsement from their undergraduate institution, typically from the university’s President, Provost, or Academic Dean. This endorsement is a crucial part of the application for international scholarships, as it reflects the institution’s confidence in the candidate’s abilities and potential to succeed.

Lastly, applicants for postgraduate scholarships UK must apply to a UK institution for their graduate studies. They need to list their first-choice university and intended courses on their Marshall Scholarship application and, if selected, must enroll in the programs they specified.

Before you begin applying for international scholarships, be sure to familiarize yourself with the eligibility criteria, requirements, and deadline for the best chances at securing funding.

## How to Apply to the Marshall Scholarship

Applying for the Marshall Scholarship is a multi-step process that requires careful planning and attention to detail. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you navigate the postgraduate scholarships UK application process:

### 4 Steps to Apply to the Marshall Scholarship

![Image 6: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/pexels-ketut-subiyanto-4560175-1024x683.jpg)
### **Step 1**

The first step is research and preparation. This includes exploring UK universities and programs to find those that align with your academic and career goals. During this time, you should familiarize yourself with the scholarship’s selection criteria including academic merit, leadership potential, and ambassadorial potential.

### **Step 2**

Next, it’s important to contact your undergraduate institution. Reach out to your university’s fellowship or scholarship office to express your interest in applying. They will guide you through the internal endorsement process, so be sure to adhere to any internal deadlines, which often precede the official Marshall Scholarship deadline. For example, the University of North Carolina ([UNC](https://honorscarolina.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Marshall-Scholarship-Timeline-1-1.pdf)) typically sets its campus endorsement application deadline in early August, while [Wellesley](https://www1.wellesley.edu/careereducation/resources/marshall-scholarship-rising-seniors-graduates) College’s deadline usually falls in mid-August.

### **Step 3**

Once you have secured institutional support from your undergraduate university, you can begin the online application through the official Marshall Scholarship portal. The application requires several key materials.

![Image 7: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/pexels-pixabay-159510-1024x575.jpg)
### **Personal Statement (750 words)**

The personal statement is your opportunity to share your story. This essay should detail your background, interests, and motivations. Admissions committees are looking for authenticity and depth, so reflect on formative experiences, challenges you have overcome, and how they have shaped your academic and personal journey. Consider what drives your intellectual curiosity and how your passions align with your future goals.

### **Proposed Academic Program Essay (500 words)**

In this essay, clearly articulate your chosen course of study in the UK and explain its relevance to your future goals. The committee wants to see that you have thoroughly researched your program and understand how it fits into your broader academic and professional trajectory.

### **Post-Scholarship Plan Essay (150 words)**

This brief essay should outline your plans after completing the scholarship. Be concise but also clear about how you intend to apply what you learned in the UK once you return home or pursue your next steps.

### **Leadership Essay (500 words)**

The Marshall Scholarship values strong leadership potential. Use this essay to highlight moments where you have taken initiative, inspired others, or created meaningful change. Consider both formal roles, like student government or organization leadership, and informal leadership like mentoring, advocacy, or leading projects.

### **Ambassadorial Potential Essay (500 words)**

As a Marshall Scholar, you’re expected to act as a bridge between the UK and the US. This essay should discuss how you plan to foster transatlantic relations, both during and after your time in the UK.

### **Three Letters of Recommendation**

You will need three recommendation letters, with at least two coming from academic references. These letters should speak to your intellectual ability, leadership qualities, and character.

### **Official Transcripts**

Submit certified copies of your academic records. Securing institutional endorsement is a crucial step. You must submit your completed application to your university’s endorsement committee by their specified deadline. The institution will then review your materials and decide whether to endorse your candidacy.

If you receive an endorsement, your university will submit your application to the Marshall Commission on your behalf. It’s essential to meet all deadlines, including the official submission date, which typically falls in late September.

### **Step 4**

The final stage is the interview process. Shortlisted candidates are usually invited for interviews in November. To prepare, review your application thoroughly and be ready to discuss your academic interests, leadership experiences, and ambassadorial potential.

Throughout the application process, it’s important to stay organized–keep all your materials in order and ensure they meet the specified requirements. Make sure to carefully follow all guidelines, as failure to do so may result in disqualification. Finally, maintain clear and timely communication with your referees and university officials to ensure every component of your application is completed on time.

By carefully following these steps and paying close attention to detail, you can strengthen your Marshall Scholarship application and stand out among other applicants for postgraduate scholarships UK.

### Marshall Scholarship General Timeline

The next application cycle usually opens in late spring, however, it’s essential to regularly check the official Marshall Scholarship website for updates on exact dates.

## What are the Marshall Scholarship application requirements?

In order to submit your application on time, you’ll need to have all the required documents. Indeed, the Marshall Scholarship application requires several key documents, including:

### Required Application Documents

![Image 8: marshall scholarship](https://www.collegeadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/pexels-george-pak-7972310-1024x683.jpg)
### **Academic transcripts:**

You’ll need to submit certified copies of your academic records. These transcripts should reflect your full academic history, including courses taken, grades received, and any honors or distinctions earned. The committee uses this to assess your intellectual ability and academic consistency.

### **CV/Resume:**

Your CV or resume should concisely highlight your academic, leadership, and extracurricular achievements. This is the document that provides a quick snapshot of your qualifications and experiences.

### **Three letters of recommendation:**

**Primary academic:**

This letter should come from a professor or research advisor who knows your academic work deeply. They should discuss your intellectual capabilities, research skills, and scholarly potential.

**General academic:**

This recommender can be another professor or mentor familiar with your broader academic or extracurricular work. They can highlight your versatility, teamwork, and how you engage with learning beyond the classroom.

**Leadership skills:**

This letter should focus on your leadership potential. It can come from a mentor, supervisor, or community leader who has witnessed you take initiative, inspire others, or create meaningful change.

### **Essays:**

**Personal statement:**

Use this essay to highlight experiences that showcase your resilience, adaptability, and purpose. Be sure to connect your personal experiences to your academic ambitions and leadership qualities.

**Study plans and post-scholarship goals:**

These essays should be used to explain how your intended program complements your past academic work and future career plans, showing why studying in the UK provides a unique advantage. You should also mention specific roles or industries you aspire to work in.

**Essays showcasing leadership and ambassadorial potential:**

Use these essays to reflect on leadership challenges you faced and how you handled them. You will also want to emphasize your diplomacy, empathy, and communication skills.

Every one of these required documents is important to your overall application. However, to truly strengthen your application, it’s important to get strong recommendations from faculty who can speak to your academic achievements, leadership abilities, and capacity to foster international understanding. Additionally, your essays should not only emphasize your academic ambitions, but also present a clear vision for how you plan to contribute to global relations.Most importantly, your letters of recommendation and essays offer an insight into your life, values, and goals that may not be seen through your academic or extracurricular achievements.

## Prepare for the Marshall Scholarship Interview

Applicants who are successful in the Marshall Scholarship application process will be invited to an interview. These interviews are typically held in mid to late November at a designated location within your application region, such as Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Houston, Los Angeles, New York City, San Francisco, or Washington, D.C.

When preparing for the interview, it’s important to be yourself. Ideally, you want to demonstrate confidence without sounding robotic, as the committee values authenticity and strong interpersonal skills. Make sure you understand the mission of the Marshall Scholarship and can clearly explain how your background and goals align with its values. Additionally, be ready to discuss experiences or qualities that may not have been fully covered in your application. The information you provide will offer a more complete picture of who you are and what you hope to achieve with this opportunity.

Most importantly, prepare for your interview. Do your homework on Marshall Scholarship interview [preparation tips](https://www.marshallscholarship.org/media/1950/marshall-interview-advice.pdf), as well as potential topics you may be asked to speak about during the 20-30 minute interview.

Jackie Knee,
2019 Marshall Sherfield Fellow

Prior to starting as the 2019 Marshall Sherfield fellow, I completed
my PhD in Environmental Engineering at the Georgia Institute of
Technology. I also hold BS and MS degrees in public health from the  Jackie Knee
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, am a returned Fulbright
Fellow, and have professional experience working as an environmental
health scientist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in
Atlanta, Georgia.

I chose to complete my Marshall Sherfield fellowship at the London
School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) for several reasons.
LSHTM is one of the best schools of public health in the world and
offered the opportunity to connect with and learn from research
leaders in my field. Further, I had established collaborative ties with
a multidisciplinary research group at LSHTM during my PhD work.
I wanted to  strengthen this  relationship while developing  my own
research niche to complement the group’s ongoing work. In short, I
saw the future of my career at LSHTM.

My primary research interests lie at the intersection of public health,
microbiology, and environmental engineering. More specifically, I
am interested in studying the environmental transmission of enteric
pathogens in vulnerable populations. To do this, I use cutting-
edge molecular and serological tools to characterise pathways of
infection and to evaluate water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)
interventions that aim to interrupt transmission. While at LSHTM,
I had the opportunity to broaden my portfolio of work, leading
microbiological analyses for several WASH-focused research studies,
and to contribute to initiatives such as the recently announced Lancet
Commission on WASH and Health. I also leveraged the opportunity
provided by the fellowship to pursue a new research avenue: the use
of pathogen-specific antibody response to measure enteric disease
transmission.

I’m happy to report that as my Marshall Sherfield fellowship ended,
I transitioned into a position as an Assistant Professor at LSHTM.
My very first PhD student started in January 2022, and I’m looking
forward to bright and productive future in London.

Jackie Knee,
2019 Marshall Sherfield Fellow

Prior to starting as the 2019 Marshall Sherfield fellow, I completed
my PhD in Environmental Engineering at the Georgia Institute of
Technology. I also hold BS and MS degrees in public health from the  Jackie Knee
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, am a returned Fulbright
Fellow, and have professional experience working as an environmental
health scientist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in
Atlanta, Georgia.

I chose to complete my Marshall Sherfield fellowship at the London
School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) for several reasons.
LSHTM is one of the best schools of public health in the world and
offered the opportunity to connect with and learn from research
leaders in my field. Further, I had established collaborative ties with
a multidisciplinary research group at LSHTM during my PhD work.
I wanted to  strengthen this  relationship while developing  my own
research niche to complement the group’s ongoing work. In short, I
saw the future of my career at LSHTM.

My primary research interests lie at the intersection of public health,
microbiology, and environmental engineering. More specifically, I
am interested in studying the environmental transmission of enteric
pathogens in vulnerable populations. To do this, I use cutting-
edge molecular and serological tools to characterise pathways of
infection and to evaluate water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)
interventions that aim to interrupt transmission. While at LSHTM,
I had the opportunity to broaden my portfolio of work, leading
microbiological analyses for several WASH-focused research studies,
and to contribute to initiatives such as the recently announced Lancet
Commission on WASH and Health. I also leveraged the opportunity
provided by the fellowship to pursue a new research avenue: the use
of pathogen-specific antibody response to measure enteric disease
transmission.

I’m happy to report that as my Marshall Sherfield fellowship ended,
I transitioned into a position as an Assistant Professor at LSHTM.
My very first PhD student started in January 2022, and I’m looking
forward to bright and productive future in London.
